decisionSection.title: When to choose modular vs containers
decisionSection.description: Modular systems and container conversions serve different budgets and scenarios. Use this guide to find your best fit.

chooseModular: You need open floor plans and freely reconfigurable training scenarios
Phased construction, later expansion, or capability upgrades are planned
Roof and floor must be rated for training loads and long-term heavy use
You want 50-year structural life with low maintenance
Training realism requires building-like layouts and heights
chooseContainer: Very short-term temporary training with low life expectancy
Extremely limited budget accepting ~15-year service life
Site constraints prevent standard modular installation
Interim solution before planned demolition and rebuild

overview.title: Why modular systems are the superior choice
overview.description: Modular systems use new materials and all-galvanized steel frames — longer life, more open space, and repeated reconfiguration that refurbished containers cannot match.
overview.lead: Containers were built for freight, not live-fire training. As training facilities, they often face corrosion, insufficient load capacity, difficult modification, and high secondary maintenance costs.
overview.body: Modular training systems are purpose-built for emergency training from day one: open floor plans, movable walls and doors, roof and floor designed for training loads — scenarios that grow freely with your mission.

rows.modular: Open floor plan, no fixed partitions, high space utilization
rows.container: Constrained by container dimensions, narrow and fixed layout

rows.modular: Freely added, removed, and rearranged for varied scenarios
rows.container: Openings require on-site cutting; changes are difficult and weaken structure

rows.modular: New materials, all-galvanized steel frame, corrosion and deformation resistant
rows.container: Refurbished used containers, plain steel prone to rust, inconsistent quality

rows.modular: Designed to training load standards, smooth transition from roof to interior
rows.container: Not load-rated; major reinforcement required for training use

rows.modular: Non-slip working surface + galvanized underside; full thermal liner in burn rooms
rows.container: Mostly hardwood floors; burn rooms with steel base only

rows.modular: Factory paint on new steel surfaces, long-lasting stability
rows.container: Repainted over old surfaces, requires periodic recoating
Welded assembly; changes require cutting and repainting

rows.modular: Modules reconfigure and stack, expand as needed
rows.container: Limited expansion; stacking and connection constraints

rows.modular: Close to real building layouts and heights
rows.container: Significant scale gap from real buildings

rows.modular: Reconfigurable and refurbishable, higher long-term value
rows.container: Modification limited, high later refurbishment cost
